members: Varenicline: α4β2 nicotinic acetylcholine receptor partial agonist (NRPA)
Bupropion SR: NDRI (10-30% DAT/NET occupancy) + non-competitive nAChR antagonist
NRT (Patch, Gum, Lozenge, Spray, Inhaler): Full nicotinic receptor agonist with non-pulsatile absorption
drug_class.mechanism: α4β2 partial agonism (Varenicline), DAT/NET reuptake inhibition + nAChR blockade (Bupropion), steady nicotinic receptor stimulation (NRT)
kinetics: Bupropion: biphasic half-life 10-14h (parent), 20-27h (6-OH-bupropion metabolite), potent CYP2D6 inhibitor, metabolized by CYP2B6
Smoking cessation reduces CYP1A2 enzyme induction, increasing blood levels of Clozapine, Olanzapine, and Haloperidol
NRT Transdermal Patch: steady delivery over 16-24 hours
drug_class.onset_of_effect: 1-2 weeks for steady state and craving reduction (Varenicline & Bupropion); minutes for short-acting NRT

items: FDA-approved for smoking cessation in adults: Varenicline, Bupropion SR, and NRT
No pharmacological agents are FDA-approved for youth under 18 years; off-label use supported by AAP
Combination NRT (patch + gum/lozenge) or NRT + Bupropion superior to monotherapy
Bupropion SR + Contingency Management (CM) significantly effective in adolescent smoking cessation
key_numbers: 0: FDA-approved cessation medications for youth under 18 years
3-4x: Increase in 1-year quit rate with Varenicline vs placebo in adults
2x: Increase in quit rate with Bupropion SR vs placebo
4.4%: Adolescent NRT abstinence rate at 12 months (vs 6.6% placebo)

items: Varenicline: Dose-dependent nausea, insomnia, vivid dreams, GI discomfort; EAGLES trial confirmed no elevated neuropsychiatric risk vs placebo
Bupropion: Insomnia, dry mouth, weight loss, anorexia, tremor, hypertension, tachycardia
Bupropion Seizure Risk: Dose-dependent; contraindicated in anorexia/bulimia nervosa and epilepsy
NRT: Patch causes local erythema/pruritus; Gum/Lozenge causes mouth/throat irritation, hiccups, nausea
key_numbers: 0.1%: Seizure risk with Bupropion at 300 mg/day
0.4%: Seizure risk with Bupropion at 400 mg/day
10x: Seizure risk increase with Bupropion doses >450 mg/day
20-50%: Local skin reaction rate with NRT patch

items: Blood pressure and heart rate baseline and periodic monitoring (especially for Bupropion and NRT combinations)
Weight and height tracking on pediatric growth charts for youth on Bupropion
Neuropsychiatric monitoring for changes in mood, agitation, anxiety, or suicidality
Biomarkers: Exhaled carbon monoxide (CO < 6-8 ppm) and cotinine levels (half-life 16-20h)
Therapeutic drug monitoring (TDM) of CYP1A2 substrates (Clozapine, Olanzapine) 1-2 weeks post-cessation
key_numbers: 6-8 ppm: Exhaled CO cutoff confirming smoking abstinence
16-20 hours: Cotinine half-life for verifying abstinence
14 days: Washout period between MAOIs and Bupropion
1-2 weeks: Timeframe to recheck Clozapine/Olanzapine levels after quitting

items: Varenicline: Start 1-2 weeks before Target Quit Date (TQD); 0.5 mg daily x3d -> 0.5 mg bid x4d -> 1 mg bid from day 8 for 12-24 weeks
Bupropion SR: Start 1-2 weeks before TQD; 150 mg daily x3d -> 150 mg bid (at least 8 hours apart); max 300 mg/day for smoking cessation
Contraindicated to crush, split, or chew Bupropion SR/XL tablets (risk of rapid release and seizure)
NRT Gum: Chew and park method for buccal absorption; avoid acidic drinks 15 minutes before/during use
Pediatric off-label use requires parental Informed Consent and adolescent Informed Assent
key_numbers: 1-2 weeks: Lead time to start Varenicline/Bupropion prior to Target Quit Date
8 hours: Minimum required interval between Bupropion SR doses
300 mg/day: Maximum daily dose of Bupropion SR for smoking cessation
15 minutes: Time to avoid acidic beverages before/during NRT gum or lozenge use

high_yield: Varenicline is an α4β2 partial agonist acting as net agonist without nicotine and net antagonist with nicotine (causing extinction).
No smoking cessation drugs are FDA-approved for under 18 years; all pediatric use is off-label.
Bupropion is strictly contraindicated in Anorexia and Bulimia Nervosa due to elevated seizure risk.
Cessation of smoking decreases CYP1A2 induction, leading to potentially toxic rises in Clozapine and Olanzapine levels.
Combination therapy (NRT patch + short-acting NRT, or NRT + Bupropion) is superior to monotherapy.
In adolescents, Bupropion SR combined with Contingency Management (CM) yields the highest abstinence rates.
